facts.statement: Yandusaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age between 168 and 162 million years ago, in eastern Asia.
facts.quote: Yandusaurus is a genus of basal neornithischian dinosaur from the middle Jurassic (Bathonian age, approximately 168 to 162 Ma) of eastern Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was accidentally processed by a composter during construction work in January 1973 near the Honghe dam in Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: In January 1973 the Museum of the Salt Industry at Zigong in Sichuan was warned that during construction activities with a composter at Jinzidang near the Honghe dam inadvertently a dinosaur skeleton had been processed.

facts.statement: Professor He Xinlu named and described the type species Yandusaurus hongheensis in 1979, after it was initially misidentified locally as Yubasaurus or Honghesaurus.
facts.quote: Though locally this animal was at first referred to as "Yubasaurus" or "Honghesaurus", in 1979 Beijing professor He Xinlu named and described it as the type species Yandusaurus hongheensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Yandusaurus is derived from Yandu, the ancient name for Zigong, which means 'salt capital' due to the area's history of salt mining.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Yandu, the ancient name for Zigong. This name is a contraction of yan, "salt", and du, "capital", occasioned by the fact that Zigong was historically the centre of Chinese salt mining.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen GCC V20501 was excavated from the Lower Shaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, GCC V20501, had been dug up in a layer of the Lower Shaximiao Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton with a skull, vertebral column, shoulder girdle, and limbs, though most elements are limited or damaged.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton with skull. Elements of most parts of the body have been preserved, the skull, vertebral column, shoulder girdle, frontlimbs and hindlimbs but all are very limited and/or damaged.

facts.statement: In 1992, Guangzhao Peng reassigned Yandusaurus multidens to the genus Agilisaurus.
facts.quote: In 1992 this was by Guangzhao Peng reassigned to the genus Agilisaurus as a A. multidens.

facts.statement: In 2005, Paul Barrett and colleagues placed Yandusaurus multidens in its own genus, Hexinlusaurus.
facts.quote: In 2005 it was by Paul Barrett e.a. placed in its own genus, Hexinlusaurus.

facts.statement: Yandusaurus had teeth with a unique pattern of parallel vertical ridges that Chinese researchers compared to the fingers of Buddha statues, which were highly asymmetrical with the inner side strongly worn down.
facts.quote: The teeth, showing a unique pattern of parallel vertical ridges compared by Chinese researchers to the fingers of the hand of Buddha statues, are very asymmetrical in that the inner side is strongly worn down.

facts.statement: The fifteen maxillary teeth of Yandusaurus were largest in the middle and overlapped.
facts.quote: The fifteen maxillary teeth are largest in the middle and overlap.

facts.statement: Yandusaurus is currently viewed as having an unresolved position within Neornithischia, as its original family Hypsilophodontidae is considered paraphyletic.
facts.quote: Today however Hypsilophodontidae is considered an unnatural (paraphyletic) group and Yandusaurus is viewed as taking an unresolved position within Neornithischia.

facts.statement: Yandusaurus is classified within the infraorder Ornithopoda.
Yandusaurus was historically assigned to the family Hypsilophodontidae.

Yandusaurus hongheensis is the only known species of the extinct genus Yandusaurus, an ornithopod that lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Yandusaurus hongheensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Yandusaurus (zhn. "lagarto de la capital de la sal") es un género representado por una sola especie de dinosaurios, ornitópodos, hipsilofodóntidos que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 165 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Juvenile specimens of Yandusaurus were small bipedal runners measuring between 1 and 1.6 meters in length, 70 centimeters in height, and weighing around 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: Fue un pequeño corredor bípedo, que tenía 5 dedos en cada mano que media entre 1 y 1,6 metros de largo 70 centímetros de alto y un peso de 7 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Yandusaurus had large eyes, as indicated by the curved jugal bone.
facts.quote: Tenía ojos grandes como lo muestra el yugal curvo.

facts.statement: Fossil occurrences of Yandusaurus are recorded from the Bajocian stage, between 170.9 and 168.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (170.9 to 168.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The lower jaws, pelvis and the end of the tail had probably been entirely destroyed by the machine.

rejected.quote: A fast-moving biped, Yandusaurus had four toes on each foot and five fingers on each hand.

rejected.statement: Yandusaurus hongheensis was considerably larger than juvenile specimens, with body length estimates ranging from 3.0 to 3.8 meters and a weight of 140 kg.
rejected.quote: Yandusaurus hongheensis was however considerably larger than these exemplars: He estimated the body length at three metres, Peng at 3.2 metres; in 2010 G.S. Paul gave an estimation of 3.8 metres length and a weight of 140 kg.
